rows.label: Gateway course: one of the two public policy gateway courses, taken in Government
rows.note: Counts Cornell GOVT courses only (exam and transfer credit left out), which also meets the rule that the gateway be taken in the Government Department.

rows.label: Methods course: one of three Government data and inquiry courses
rows.note: Exam and transfer credit left out, as for the other rows.

rows.label: Three elective courses from the Government policy electives
rows.note: The page points to an eligible list it does not print, so the board counts only fixed-credit GOVT courses numbered 3000-4999 of 3+ credits, leaving out writing seminars, intro surveys, honors thesis and independent study. That may be stricter than the list; the confirm row asks you to check each elective. A policy course from another department needs advisor approval and is not counted (see the confirm row). The optional grouping pathway is not encoded.

rows.label: Check that each elective is on the minor's eligible list of policy courses
rows.note: The board counts only upper-level Government courses of three or more credits; the department list decides which actually count, and a lower-level course on that list needs your advisor to confirm it.

rows.label: At most one course may come from another department, with advisor approval; at least four of five stay in Government
rows.note: The board counts GOVT courses only, so a non-Government policy course (up to one, approved by your advisor) is not counted until you confirm it.

rows.label: Earn a C+ or better in every course that counts toward the minor
Complete at least 15 credits for the minor
rows.note: Five courses of three credits give 15; confirm if any course carries fewer credits.
